venues.name: Fairmont Pacific Rim
venues.note: Vancouver's defining modern grand hotel, glass and art above the harbour, faced to the sea and the mountains beyond.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025), hotel and spa

venues.name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia
venues.note: A restored 1927 landmark of old-Hollywood glamour, dark wood, a saltwater infinity pool, and the city's most storied address.

venues.name: Shangri-La Vancouver
venues.note: The city's tallest tower turned discreet luxury house, spacious rooms, Asian calm, MO-standard service.

venues.name: Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
venues.note: A family-owned European jewel on Robson Square, antiques, Persian rugs, and Vancouver's most personal service.

venues.name: Loden Hotel
venues.note: A polished boutique hideaway on the quiet edge of Coal Harbour, mid-century calm with harbour and mountain light.

venues.name: The Douglas, Autograph Collection
venues.note: A design-led tower rising from the Parq entertainment complex, warm cedar, mountain views, and a private urban garden.

venues.name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
venues.note: The green-roofed 'Castle in the City' since 1939, a chateau-style landmark at the heart of downtown.

venues.name: Pan Pacific Vancouver
venues.note: Perched over Canada Place under the white sails, the definitive harbour-front address, ships and seaplanes at the door.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2025 (Best Hotels in Canada)

venues.name: JW Marriott Parq Vancouver
venues.note: The polished flagship of the Parq complex, contemporary rooms above a rooftop park and a cluster of restaurants.

venues.name: AnnaLena
venues.note: Playful, precise contemporary cooking in a warm West-Side room, Vancouver at its most confidently modern.

venues.name: Barbara
venues.note: A tiny, ingredient-obsessed counter in Chinatown, a personal tasting menu of quiet intensity.

venues.name: Burdock & Co
venues.note: Andrea Carlson's seasonal, farm-driven cooking, Pacific Northwest terroir on a plate.

venues.name: iDen & QuanJuDe Beijing Duck House
venues.note: The famed Beijing duck house brought to Vancouver, lacquered Peking duck of real ceremony.

venues.name: Kissa Tanto
venues.note: A moody, 1960s-Tokyo-jazz-bar room serving singular Japanese-Italian cooking, one of the city's most-loved tables.

venues.name: Masayoshi
venues.note: Masayoshi Baba's serene sushi counter, exacting edomae craft away from the downtown crowds.

venues.name: Okeya Kyujiro
venues.note: A theatrical kaiseki-and-sushi experience under lantern light, dining as performance.

venues.name: Published on Main
venues.note: The city's most celebrated modern room, refined, seasonal cooking on buzzing Main Street.

venues.name: St. Lawrence
venues.note: A Québécois-French bistro dressed as a Montréal railway diner, hearty, exact, deeply comforting.

venues.name: Sumibiyaki Arashi
venues.note: An intimate charcoal-grill counter, yakitori and sumibiyaki cooked with quiet precision.

venues.name: Sushi Hyun
venues.note: A minimalist omakase counter of great purity, fish flown in and treated with reverence.

venues.name: Sushi Masuda
venues.note: A Tokyo-trained master's edomae counter, classical sushi of quiet, uncompromising standard.

venues.name: Botanist
venues.note: Modern Canadian cooking inside the Fairmont Pacific Rim, polished, seasonal, and beautifully served.

venues.name: Vij's
venues.note: Vikram Vij's landmark of modern Indian cooking, the restaurant that reimagined Indian food in Canada.

venues.name: Karma Indian Bistro
venues.note: Refined, generous Indian cooking that earned Michelin's value nod, warm and familiar for Indian palates.

venues.name: Anh and Chi
venues.note: Beloved, beautifully run modern Vietnamese on Main, family-owned and full of heart.

venues.name: Phnom Penh
venues.note: The legendary Cambodian-Vietnamese room, its butter beef and chicken wings are a Vancouver rite of passage.

venues.name: Fable Kitchen
venues.note: Honest farm-to-table cooking on West 4th, rustic, seasonal and consistently good.

venues.name: The Lunch Lady
venues.note: A Vancouver homage to Saigon's famous street-food matriarch, bright, punchy Vietnamese.

venues.name: Good Thief
venues.note: An inventive, value-driven room that won Michelin's newest nod on Main, bold and unexpected.

venues.name: Stanley Park Seawall
venues.note: A 9-kilometre paved rim traces the peninsula between old-growth forest and the sea, past the Lions Gate Bridge, English Bay and the downtown skyline. Have your guide arrange a private cycle or a slow morning stroll before the crowds; grandparents and children keep the same flat, car-free path.

venues.name: Brockton Point Totem Poles
venues.note: Nine towering First Nations poles stand in a meadow near the water, some carved as early as the 1880s and among the most-photographed sights in British Columbia. A small interpretive centre explains the Kwakwaka'wakw and Haida stories behind them, a gentle first read on Indigenous culture for a multi-generation group.

venues.name: Prospect Point
venues.note: The high bluff at the park's north tip looks straight onto the Lions Gate Bridge and the Burrard Inlet, with a cafe and gift shop for a pause. It is the classic photo-stop on a private drive around the park.

venues.name: Vancouver Aquarium
venues.note: Set inside Stanley Park, Canada's largest aquarium runs sea otters, jellies and a rainforest gallery that reliably holds young children for hours. A calm, indoor option when the coast turns grey.

venues.name: Lost Lagoon
venues.note: A tranquil freshwater lake at the park's edge, ringed by a level trail where herons and swans gather at dusk. A quiet, unhurried loop for grandparents who want the park without the full seawall.

venues.name: Granville Island Public Market
venues.note: An indoor food hall under the Granville Bridge where farm stalls, Oyama Sausage, Benton Brothers cheese and Belgian chocolatiers sit beside fresh-off-the-boat seafood. A private tasting walk here is the easiest, most delicious hour in the city, with plenty for vegetarians.

venues.name: Granville Island artisan studios & galleries
venues.note: Beyond the market, the island's converted warehouses hold glass-blowers, potters, a sake maker and independent galleries. A relaxed browse for a collector, walkable and free of traffic.

venues.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
venues.note: A 137-metre cable bridge sways 70 metres above the Capilano River canyon, with a Treetops walk strung between 1,300-year-old Douglas firs and a glass Cliffwalk cantilevered off the rock. The engineered thrill everyone photographs; a private driver spares you the North Shore parking scrum.

venues.name: Grouse Mountain
venues.note: The Skyride gondola climbs to an alpine playground with 360-degree city and ocean views, a resident pair of grizzlies named Grinder and Coola, a lumberjack show and the Eye of the Wind turbine you can stand beneath. A single mountain that fills a whole family day, dawn to dusk.
credentials: Eye of the Wind, a glass viewing pod set just below the blades of a working wind turbine, billed as the only one of its kind.

venues.name: Lynn Canyon Park & Suspension Bridge
venues.note: A free 50-metre suspension bridge over a rainforest gorge with waterfalls and swimming holes, the local's quieter answer to Capilano. Bring a private guide and you get temperate rainforest with none of the ticket-gate crowds.

venues.name: Gastown & the Steam Clock
venues.note: Vancouver's oldest quarter, all cobblestones and Victorian brick, anchored by the whistling steam clock that puffs Westminster chimes on the quarter-hour. Boutiques, First Nations galleries and some of the city's best restaurants line the same few blocks.

venues.name: Chinatown
venues.note: One of North America's largest historic Chinatowns, with the ornate Millennium Gate, herbalists and a growing wave of new restaurants and bars. Best explored on foot with a guide who can read the layers of old and new.

venues.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
venues.note: A walled Ming Dynasty scholar's garden of jade water, limestone and pavilions, the first full classical Chinese garden built outside China. A pocket of stillness in the middle of the city, marking its 40th year in 2026.
credentials: The first authentic classical Chinese garden built outside of China, opened in 1986.

venues.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
venues.note: Arthur Erickson's soaring Great Hall of glass and concrete frames towering totem poles, canoes and works from Haida, Nisga'a and Coast Salish nations, reopened in 2024 after a seismic rebuild. It holds the world's largest collection of Bill Reid, including his masterwork The Raven and the First Men.
credentials: Home to the world's largest collection of works by Haida artist Bill Reid.

venues.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
venues.note: The city's flagship gallery, beside Robson Square, holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr, the painter of British Columbia's forests and Indigenous villages. Through 2026 it shows its largest Carr exhibition in over twenty years.
credentials: Holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr's work.

venues.name: Canada Place & the waterfront
venues.note: The white sail-roofed cruise pier juts into Burrard Inlet with a seawall promenade, the Canadian Trail interpretive walk and float planes taking off from the harbour. An easy, level introduction to the city's water-meets-mountains setting.

venues.name: FlyOver Canada
venues.note: A flight-simulator ride inside Canada Place that suspends you before a 20-metre dome screen and sweeps you coast to coast with wind, mist and scent. Eight thrilling minutes that delight children and grandparents alike, whatever the weather outside.

venues.name: Science World
venues.note: The mirrored geodesic dome at the head of False Creek, built for Expo 86, is a hands-on science centre with an OMNIMAX dome theatre and floors of experiments for curious kids. Its 391 lights run programmed sequences over the water every night.

venues.name: English Bay Beach
venues.note: The city's most beloved downtown beach, where locals gather for sunsets over the freighters and the summer fireworks. Steps from West End restaurants, an easy stroll for an evening with the family.

venues.name: Kitsilano Beach
venues.note: A wide sandy beach backed by lawns, tennis courts and Vancouver's landmark 137-metre saltwater pool, framed by mountain and skyline views. The heart of laid-back "Kits", ringed by good cafes and yoga-set shops.

venues.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
venues.note: A former rock quarry transformed into the city's most-visited park, crowning Vancouver's highest point with formal flower gardens and a panorama of downtown against the North Shore mountains. A gentle, manicured green space for a slow multi-generation afternoon.

venues.name: Bloedel Conservatory
venues.note: A glass dome atop Queen Elizabeth Park holding tropical, subtropical and desert zones under one roof, with free-flying parrots and koi. A warm, colourful refuge on a rainy day, small enough not to tire anyone.

venues.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
venues.note: A 22-hectare garden of 7,500 plant species across sixty themed sections, with an Elizabethan hedge maze and a striking undulating-roof visitor centre. Serene and never crowded, ideal for a private morning wander.

venues.name: Lonsdale Quay & the SeaBus crossing
venues.note: Ride the SeaBus twelve minutes across the harbour for one of the great cheap skyline views, landing at a lively public market and the neon Shipyards district. A short, scenic outing that feels like a proper voyage to the children.

venues.name: Commercial Drive
venues.note: The city's old Italian quarter, now a bohemian stretch of espresso bars, patios and independent shops known simply as "The Drive". A neighbourhood to wander for anyone who wants the real, unpolished Vancouver.

venues.name: Punjabi Market (Little India)
venues.note: The stretch of Main Street between 49th and 51st that has been Vancouver's Little India since the 1970s, with sari shops, sweet houses and institutions like the Himalaya Restaurant. A nostalgic, homely detour for Indian families, quieter now that much of the community has moved to Surrey.

venues.name: Surrey & the South Asian food belt
venues.note: Home to one of the largest Punjabi communities outside India, Surrey's Newton and Payal Business Centre serve the region's most authentic Punjabi, Gujarati and South Indian cooking, plus gurdwaras and sweet shops. Worth a private car trip for a homesick, food-loving multi-gen group.

venues.name: Aberdeen Centre & the Golden Village
venues.note: Richmond's Golden Village is one of North America's densest concentrations of Asian malls and restaurants, with Aberdeen Centre's food court and bubble-tea culture the anchor. A vegetarian-friendly, kid-pleasing crash course in Hong Kong and Taiwanese food.

venues.name: Richmond Night Market
venues.note: The largest night market in North America, over a hundred stalls and 500-plus dishes of hawker-style Asian street food under strings of lights, running weekend evenings from spring to September. A festive, sensory night out for all ages; a private driver makes the far-out location painless.
credentials: The largest night market in North America.

venues.name: Steveston Village
venues.note: A historic fishing village where you can buy salmon and crab straight off the boats at Fisherman's Wharf, tour a heritage cannery and stroll a boardwalk to the river's mouth. A charming, low-key half-day with genuine maritime character.

venues.name: Sea-to-Sky Gondola
venues.note: A ten-minute climb above Howe Sound to a summit lodge with a viewing platform, a suspension bridge and alpine trails looking over turquoise fjord water. The quieter, more natural alternative to Whistler's Peak 2 Peak, an hour up the coast.

venues.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway drive
venues.note: One of the world's great coastal drives, hugging the Howe Sound fjord from Vancouver past Shannon Falls and Squamish up to Whistler. With a private driver it becomes a leisurely day of turnouts, waterfalls and photographs rather than a slog.

venues.name: Shannon Falls
venues.note: British Columbia's third-highest waterfall at 335 metres, a short flat walk from the Sea-to-Sky Highway to a viewing platform in the spray. A five-minute stop that feels like a proper wilderness moment.

venues.name: Whistler Village
venues.note: A pedestrian alpine resort of cobbled lanes, patios and boutiques ninety minutes north, framed by two ski mountains and buzzing summer and winter alike. The natural base for a mountain day, or an overnight for a longer stay.

venues.name: Bowen Island
venues.note: A twenty-minute ferry from Horseshoe Bay lands you at Snug Cove, an artist's island of cafes, galleries, sandy coves and fifty kilometres of forest trails with no chain in sight. Vancouver's closest island escape, easy and unhurried for a half-day.

venues.name: Cypress Mountain lookout
venues.note: A short mountain drive above West Vancouver ends at a lookout that takes in the whole city, the Gulf Islands and, on a clear day, Mount Baker across the border. The best sunset panorama within twenty minutes of downtown.

venues.name: Deep Cove
venues.note: A postcard cove tucked into the fjord where you can rent a kayak on calm water, walk the Quarry Rock trail for a view, and reward the effort with a famous Honey's doughnut. A gentle, pretty morning off the tourist trail.

venues.name: Nitobe Memorial Garden
venues.note: A serene Japanese stroll-and-tea garden on the UBC campus, considered one of the most authentic outside Japan, with a tea house, koi and maples that blaze in autumn. A meditative counterpoint to the nearby Museum of Anthropology.

venues.name: Grouse Grind trail
venues.note: A relentless 2.9-kilometre staircase up the face of Grouse Mountain, known as "Mother Nature's Stairmaster", that fit visitors climb before riding the gondola back down. For the athletic member of the party who wants a real challenge with a view.

venues.name: Second Beach & Ceperley Meadow
venues.note: A family beach on the Stanley Park seawall with a heated outdoor pool, a playground and a big grassy meadow for a picnic. The easiest spot to let children loose while adults take in the sea view.

venues.name: Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre
venues.note: A glass elevator shoots up to a 360-degree observation deck 168 metres over downtown, taking in the harbour, Stanley Park and the mountains in one turn. The quickest way to orient a group on their first day.

venues.name: Robson Street shopping
venues.note: The city's flagship shopping promenade, running from the art gallery toward Stanley Park, mixing global luxury names with cafes and people-watching patios. The obvious stroll for a retail afternoon downtown.

venues.name: Mount Seymour
venues.note: The least-visited of the three North Shore peaks, a quieter drive up to alpine meadows, easy family trails in summer and gentle ski slopes in winter, all with a broad valley view. The insider's choice when Grouse feels too busy.

venues.name: Yaletown
venues.note: A former warehouse district turned polished waterfront neighbourhood of loading-dock patios, design shops and marina views onto False Creek. The stylish quarter for an evening of dinner and a stroll along the seawall.

venues.name: Botanist Bar
venues.note: The bar inside Vancouver's only Forbes Five-Star hotel, botanically-driven cocktails and the city's highest-ranked drinking room.
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 26), highest Vancouver entry

venues.name: The Keefer Bar
venues.note: An apothecary-themed cocktail den inspired by Chinatown's historic herbalists, dark, aromatic and thrilling.
credentials: Named Best Bar in Canada on the 2025 list

venues.name: Prophecy
venues.note: A refined, low-lit cocktail room bringing serious drinks and hospitality to Gastown, a rising Vancouver name.
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 53, extended list)

venues.name: Laowai
venues.note: A hidden 1920s-Shanghai speakeasy behind a freezer door, velvet, brass and glamour, and drinks to match.
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 67, extended list)
Named Best New Bar in Canada (2022)

venues.name: Meo
venues.note: An inventive, intimate cocktail bar with a devoted following, one of the city's newest 50-Best names.
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 92, extended list)

venues.name: 1927 Lobby Lounge, Rosewood Hotel Georgia
venues.note: A jewel-box hotel lounge under the restored 1927 ceiling, the city's most glamorous nightcap.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key hotel, a restored 1927 landmark

venues.name: Bacchus, Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
venues.note: A clubby, wood-panelled piano bar in a Relais & Châteaux house, Vancouver's most European nightcap.
credentials: Inside a Relais & Châteaux, MICHELIN One-Key hotel

venues.name: Reflections, The Rooftop, The Douglas
venues.note: A garden terrace above the Parq complex, fire pits, greenery and open-air drinks over the city.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Guide selected hotel, a seasonal urban-garden rooftop
